newsitem.title: UK: Deutsche's MGAM seeks to reassure clients.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche's MGAM seeks to reassure clients.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) has written 1,000 letters to pension fund clients stating there would be no more staff departures and insiting all managers were "entirely loyal to the business", the Financial Times reported in its Saturday edition.

The paper said MGAM's chief executive Robert Smith expected to lose some of the pension contracts directly managed by Nicola Horlick, who was suspended and then resigned this week, but that he believed there was "a lot of support" for its stance.
Nevertheless, the Financial Times said the firm had launched "an intensive marketing campaign" to reassure its clients. Each letter was signed by a director and fund manager, it said.
The ex-head of pension fund business at MGAM was suspended pending an internal investigation into what the firm called "a potential breach of her contract." She resigned on Thursday.
The Daily Telegraph said Smith had considered Horlick as his possible successor before her high-profile departure this week.

"I had several discussions with Nicola in October about a wider role for her. If you really pushed me, I'd say that I viewed her as my potential successor in two to three years," the Telegraph quoted Smith as saying.
